message.content:
You are doing PUBLIC-WEB UX research only. Do NOT read, touch, or reference any local repository (especially /opt/nxeon). Do NOT write any files. Return all findings as your final text message.

Study the CURRENT (2025–2026) customer-facing UX of: Hetzner (both Cloud Console at console.hetzner.cloud and Robot for dedicated servers), Vercel, Render, Railway, and Coolify (self-hosted PaaS). Use WebSearch and WebFetch on official docs (docs.hetzner.com, docs.hetzner.cloud, vercel.com/docs, vercel.com/changelog, render.com/docs, render.com/changelog, docs.railway.com, railway.com/changelog, coolify.io/docs), product-tour pages, changelogs, help-center articles, and reputable UX teardowns/reviews. Where a source is not fetchable, say so explicitly rather than inventing.

For EACH provider capture concisely, with the source URL for each claim:
1. PURCHASE/DEPLOY FLOW: exact step order (Hetzner Cloud: location -> image -> type -> networking -> SSH keys -> volumes -> firewalls -> backups -> placement groups -> labels -> cloud config -> name -> "Create & Buy now"; verify exact current order and CTA). What is decided BEFORE payment vs after; new-account verification (Hetzner's ID/identity verification and payment-method setup; Vercel/Render/Railway free tiers, trial credits, hobby vs pro, card requirement); defaults and "recommended" markers; progressive disclosure (collapsed sections); region selection style (flags list, map, latency); plan presentation (Hetzner's shared vs dedicated vCPU tabs and Arm/x86; Vercel's Hobby/Pro/Enterprise; Render's instance types table; Railway's usage-based pricing with resource sliders); CTA wording; whether checkout is inline vs separate; payment methods; promo/credit handling.
2. PRICE TRANSPARENCY: hourly/monthly, monthly caps, running cost estimate in the wizard, IPv4 add-on fee surfacing, taxes/VAT display, usage-based estimates (Railway's estimated monthly cost, Vercel's usage dashboards and spend management), renewal vs intro pricing.
3. POST-DEPLOY / PROVISIONING: what the user sees while provisioning or building (Vercel's build logs + deployment status timeline "Building -> Deploying -> Ready"; Render's deploy logs and events; Railway's build/deploy logs; Coolify's deployment logs; Hetzner's server "initializing" state); success moment (Vercel's deployment success screen with preview screenshot and "Visit"/"Assign domain"); first-run onboarding (Vercel's "Add domain" prompt, Render's dashboard checklist, Railway's templates, Hetzner's console and SSH guidance). Time-to-first-value guidance.
4. MANAGEMENT IA: single-resource page structure (identity header, primary actions, tab order); danger zone placement (Vercel/Render/Railway "Danger Zone" at settings bottom, Hetzner "Delete" tab); dashboard home for returning users (Vercel's project grid with recent deployments, Railway's canvas/project view, Render's services list, Hetzner's project switcher); command palette / global search (Vercel Cmd+K with categories, Railway Cmd+K, Render search); notifications/alerts; activity/audit logs (Hetzner activity feed; Vercel activity log).
5. DOMAIN & DNS: Vercel's domain add flow (add domain -> shows DNS/nameserver instructions -> "Valid configuration" check -> auto SSL), Render custom domains flow, Railway custom domains, Hetzner DNS console; propagation/verification feedback patterns.
6. TRUST & ERROR PATTERNS: destructive confirmation (Vercel type-project-name-to-delete; Hetzner's delete flow; Railway/Render delete confirmations); error message wording; status page integration; empty states; mobile behavior; 2FA prompts.
7. Notable 2025–2026 UX changes from changelogs (e.g. Vercel new dashboard/navigation, Railway's new UI, Render's new dashboard, Hetzner console redesign).

OUTPUT FORMAT: Markdown, one H2 section per provider, bullets under the seven headings, each bullet ending with the source URL in parentheses. Then a short H2 "Cross-cutting observations for PaaS/deploy UX" (5–10 bullets), especially on how deploy-first products make "intent -> running thing" fast and how they treat provisioning progress as a first-class experience. Target 1,800–2,800 words. Be concrete (exact labels, step names, CTA text). Mark anything unverified as "UNVERIFIED".
